name: Native article
look_note: The source map ends in a reader comment thread. No look renders comments, and writer-made comments would be invented testimonials, so the thread maps onto the renderer's pull-quote band (verified review quotes only) and the FAQ; the advertisement label is the tenant's disclosure_label and the byline comes from the tenant's authors.

sources.name: DTC native advertorial: editorial frame, beats that earn the product turn

sections.hero: Editorial-style headline and dek; the dek opens on the reader's problem, not the product.
sections.items: Numbered article beats that earn the product turn by item 4.
sections.faq: The questions a skeptical reader would post as comments, answered from verified facts.
sections.closing: Restate the problem and the turn in three bullets.

items.heading_hint: A familiar everyday scene where the problem shows up
Why the usual fix does not stick
What a real fix needs to do, in plain words
The product turn, with a verified fact
What everyday use looks like -- no outcome promises

voice: Editorial, plain and calm; third or second person; never the author's own first-person story.
compliance: Every number, price, spec or outcome needs a verified claim_id; a hint is never a fact.
No health or outcome promise for the product; a health statement cites the study and its population.
Never invent a publication, a reporter, an expert, a reader comment or a reviewer name.
A quote is the ad speaker's own words, framed as attributed, or a verified review the renderer places.
writer_brief: A short native article in numbered beats: problem, why the usual fix fails, what a fix needs, the product turn, everyday use. No comments section -- answer objections in the FAQ.
